::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** April 29th [1884-91?]  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** UCLA: collection 100: box 95
:::

My dear [Fanny](people/person_1151.qmd)

I am afraid this is not exactly in the line of the substance of the [Packet](organizations/other_52.qmd). I wonder if [Miss Maclean](people/person_2325.qmd) would think it worthwhile to pay for it at the rate of 1/ for twenty words and have it put into the advertisement part, in which case she had better send it straight to the publisher.

Eton was a great undertaking. I hope you prospered, and are quite well again. Poor [Gertrude](people/person_1462.qmd) has been having a bad attack of German measles, not a good addition to her other troubles. In fact if I went on it would be a list of ailments but [Julian](people/person_1624.qmd) seems really to have rather gained than lost ground.

Your affectionate cousin
C M Yonge

---

**Note:** The letter contains no message to Fanny Patteson's half-sister Joanna, so probably post-dates the latter's death in June 1884.  It was certainly written before the death of Julian Yonge in October 1891.
